scenes.text: In 1969, astronauts left a seismometer on the Moon and struck it like a bell.
scenes.art_prompt: the Moon's grey surface with a small scientific instrument, Earth small in the black sky

scenes.text: The Moon rang for nearly an hour. A dry, cracked world should not ring at all.
scenes.art_prompt: seismic waves rippling across a lunar plain, glowing rings on grey dust, illustration

scenes.text: Scientists called it a miracle of dry rock. It made the Moon sound hollow.
scenes.art_prompt: a cutaway of the Moon glowing faintly from within, surreal physics illustration

scenes.text: Then the records were re-read, decades later, by people with better tools.
scenes.art_prompt: an old reel of seismic tape under a single desk lamp, dust in the light

scenes.text:
The Moon did not ring once.
It rang twice - and the second ring started before the first one hit.
scenes.art_prompt: a calm Moon from orbit with a faint second echo of light around it, quiet conclusion
Earth rising over the lunar horizon, vast and quiet, final wide shot
